newsitem.title: USA: SEC votes to propose US investment adviser rules.
newsitem.headline: SEC votes to propose US investment adviser rules.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission voted to propose rules that would divide responsibility for regulating investment advisers between the federal government and states.

The draft regulations, which will be published for comment shortly in the Federal Register, would implement provisions of securities law reform legislatton approved by Congress in September and signed by President Clinton on October 11.
The new law gives states the primary responsibility for regulating smaller advisers that are likely to have local businesses.
And it gives SEC primary oversight of large advisers whose activities are likely to affect national markets.
Generally, advisers with $25 million or more of "assets under management" and professionals that advise investment companies, will register only with SEC, the draft rule will say.
Advisers with less than $25 million of assets under management will register with states. SEC is required to enact the changes by April 9, 1997, the rule will say..
SEC's proposed rules will tell advisers how to calculate the amount of assets they have under management and require them to report annually to the SEC any major change in their status.
The rules also would make clear how advisers are to count clients for purposes of the new law and would define key terms like "place of business."
